**Observations:**
- Affected part: Leaf (tomato leaf shape)
- Spots: Small, dark brown to black, roughly circular, scattered uniformly across the leaf surface
- Leaf remains mostly green with no large necrotic zones
- No concentric ring / target-board pattern (rules out Early Blight)
- No obvious gray/tan centers with pycnidia (less consistent with Septoria)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- Spots are small, discrete, and dark — characteristic of bacterial speck
- Some spots show a slightly raised, water-soaked-to-dark transition consistent with bacterial lesions

**Reasoning through top candidates:**
- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Small (1–3 mm), dark brown/black spots on green tomato leaves, often slightly raised, scattered — matches well
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Spots usually have a lighter grayish center with dark border — not clearly visible here
- **Early_Blight**: Requires concentric ring target pattern — absent here
- **Leaf_Mold**: Would show yellowing on upper surface, mold on underside — not evident

The small, discrete, dark spots uniformly scattered on a predominantly green tomato leaf most strongly match **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**.
